message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on North Carolina Avenue in the auction.

The current bid is $97. I have $726 in cash and a pink monopoly with four houses on each property. I am considering whether to raise to $98.

p1 owns the dark blue monopoly with heavy building. Boardwalk has four houses and Park Place has three, generating over $2,800 in rent. p4 has cash of $763 and a light blue monopoly with four houses each.

I will bid up to $150 for North Carolina Avenue. That is the property's mortgage value, which lets me deny p4 a second green and mortgage back immediately if I win. The current bid of $97 is well below that cap.

p4 has been matching every bid by one dollar. They already own the mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue, so North Carolina Avenue would give them two of three greens. Pacific Avenue is mortgaged and owned by p1, who is cash-poor but owns a devastating dark blue monopoly. p4 likely wants to trade for the green set later. I am now questioning why I should deny them this property.

I will bid to prevent p4 from completing a green monopoly. If I win, the greens stay split between us and p1. The housing shortage is real: zero houses remain in the bank. All 32 houses are already placed.

Bidding $98 nets me $52 cash after mortgaging. I am considering a jump bid to end the auction quickly.

I will stick to the minimum raise rather than jumping. A jump bid risks overpaying or paying more than necessary if the opponent drops out.

I also calculated my cash needs. Selling all twelve pink houses returns $600, but combined with $726 in cash I still fall short of the $1,700 rent on Boardwalk with four houses. I would need to mortgage properties as well.

Mortgaging the pink properties is impossible while they have four houses, so all twelve would need to be sold first. The dark blue monopolies are the real danger: Park Place with three houses pays $1,100 and Boardwalk with four pays $1,700. I am currently on the mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue, so no rent is due. Keeping cash high is essential to survive those landings.
